subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: Should empty-plugin-scope reloads preserve previously registered agent harnesses, and if so should preservation be limited to approved always-on harnesses rather than all plugin-owned harnesses?
rationale: Source inspection proves the lifecycle gap, but the correct contract affects plugin disablement, provider routing, channel delivery, and security boundaries, so automation should not choose restore-all versus ownership-aware clearing by itself.

options.title: Preserve Only Approved Always-On Harnesses
options.body: Filter any restore path to the maintainer-approved always-on harness contract and prove disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses are cleared in loader and gateway tests.

options.title: Accept Restore-All Semantics
options.body: Allow every prior harness to survive an empty active registry, but document and test that intentional compatibility/security tradeoff before merge.

options.title: Replace With Broader Lifecycle Repair
options.body: Pause the current candidate PR and design a broader plugin runtime lifecycle repair that handles empty scopes, atomic restore, and missing-runtime diagnostics together.

recommendation.title: Preserve Only Approved Always-On Harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter any restore path to the maintainer-approved always-on harness contract and prove disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses are cleared in loader and gateway tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the pluggable harness registry and is the strongest routing candidate for deciding the long-term harness ownership contract.
